observations:
Torah #173 is a very short teaching (8 lines) with only 3 bechina edges in the dataset, yielding 5 nodes in a single merged package. Even accounting for the 4 additional bechina-concepts identified in the gap analysis (אנכי, שכינתא פנימיות, שכינתא חיצוניות, כתב), all proposed additions belong to the same conceptual domain — the innermost dimension of the soul/faith — and integrate naturally into Package 1 (אֱמוּנָה וּפְנִימִיּוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ).

No independent domain of 3+ bechina-connected concepts exists outside the main cluster. The teaching's structure is a single radial cluster around one core identification (soul = faith = Keter = כ'), not a multi-package architecture.

The teaching's argument is eitza-driven rather than bechina-multiplied: Package 1 (soul/faith/Keter/כ') is the single bechina-cluster, and the teaching's eitza logic runs: [writing/speech as instrument] → [reveals soul-inwardness to the tzaddik] → [tzaddik recognizes the writer's faith-root]. The outer/inner Shekhinah distinction (שכינתא חיצוניות vs. שכינתא פנימיות) is presented as a gradation within the same domain (אני/אנכי as lesser vs. greater expressions of the same soul-revelation), not as a new independent conceptual package.

No evil-mirror package exists in this Torah. The teaching is entirely positive — it describes the capacity of writing and speech to reveal the innermost holiness of the soul. No concept in this Torah belongs to the domain of evil or the sitra achra.
